::: {#sol-constant-prediction-decompose-part2}

Add and subtract $\mean$ inside the [square](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-square):

$$
\E{\sqf{Y - c}}
= \E{\sqf{(Y - \mean) + (\mean - c)}} .
$$

Expand the square, using the [square of a sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#thm-square-of-a-sum):

$$
= \E{\sqf{Y - \mean} + 2 (Y - \mean)(\mean - c) + \sqf{\mean - c}} .
$$

Apply [linearity of expectation](expectation.qmd#thm-linearity-expectation).
The numbers $\mean$ and $c$ are [constant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-constant-function)s,
so $2(\mean - c)$ and $\sqf{\mean - c}$ come outside the expectation:

$$
= \E{\sqf{Y - \mean}} + 2 (\mean - c) \E{Y - \mean} + \sqf{\mean - c} .
$$

The middle expectation is zero,
because

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{Y - \mean} &= \E{Y} - \mean \\
&= \mean - \mean \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so the [squared-error risk](expectation.qmd#def-squared-error-risk) reduces to:

$$
= \E{\sqf{Y - \mean}} + \sqf{\mean - c} .
$$

The first term is the [variance of $Y$](#thm-variance-expanded):

$$
= \Var{Y} + \sqf{\mean - c} .
$$

:::
